articles.title: ISUP grade groups and the Gleason score

sections.heading: What a grade group is
sections.body: The International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) grade group summarises the Gleason grading of prostate cancer in five groups, from grade group 1 (lowest grade) to grade group 5 (highest grade). The system was agreed at the 2014 ISUP consensus conference. It is used together with the Gleason score, for example Gleason score 3+3=6 (grade group 1).

sections.heading: How Gleason scores map to grade groups
sections.body: Grade group 1: Gleason score 6 or less (3+3). Grade group 2: Gleason score 3+4=7. Grade group 3: Gleason score 4+3=7. Grade group 4: Gleason score 8 (4+4, 3+5 or 5+3). Grade group 5: Gleason score 9 or 10.

sections.heading: Grade groups in this app
sections.body: When a pathologist records a slide review, the server works out the grade group from the primary and secondary Gleason patterns using this table. An AI grade group, once a trained model provides one, is decision support only and never replaces the pathologist's review.

sources.name: Epstein JI et al. The 2014 ISUP Consensus Conference on Gleason Grading of Prostatic Carcinoma. Am J Surg Pathol. 2016;40(2):244-252.

sections.heading: What PI-RADS is
sections.body: PI-RADS (Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System) version 2.1 is the standard way to report multiparametric prostate MRI. Each lesion is given an assessment category from 1 to 5 for the likelihood of clinically significant cancer.

sections.heading: The five categories
sections.body: PI-RADS 1: very low (clinically significant cancer is highly unlikely). PI-RADS 2: low (clinically significant cancer is unlikely). PI-RADS 3: intermediate (the presence of clinically significant cancer is equivocal). PI-RADS 4: high (clinically significant cancer is likely). PI-RADS 5: very high (clinically significant cancer is highly likely).

sections.heading: PI-RADS in this app
sections.body: The PI-RADS category is entered with the screening record and is one of the clinical values sent to the AI analysis. It is the radiologist's category, not an AI output.

sources.name: Turkbey B et al. Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System Version 2.1: 2019 Update of PI-RADS Version 2. Eur Urol. 2019;76(3):340-351.

articles.title: PSA density and the free-to-total PSA ratio

sections.heading: PSA density
sections.body: PSA density is the serum PSA (ng/mL) divided by the prostate volume (mL), with the volume usually measured on MRI or transrectal ultrasound. It adjusts PSA for the size of the gland, because a larger prostate releases more PSA. When both values are recorded, the server calculates it. Decision thresholds differ between guidelines, so follow the local protocol.

sections.heading: Free-to-total PSA ratio
sections.body: The free-to-total PSA ratio (percentage of free PSA) is free PSA divided by total PSA. In men with a total PSA between 4 and 10 ng/mL and a benign-feeling prostate, a lower percentage of free PSA was associated with a higher risk of prostate cancer. When both values are recorded, the server calculates the ratio. Cut-offs differ between laboratories and guidelines.

sources.name: Benson MC et al. Prostate specific antigen density: a means of distinguishing benign prostatic hypertrophy and prostate cancer. J Urol. 1992;147(3 Pt 2):815-816.
Catalona WJ et al. Use of the percentage of free prostate-specific antigen to enhance differentiation of prostate cancer from benign prostatic disease. JAMA. 1998;279(19):1542-1547.

sections.heading: DRE findings recorded in this app
sections.body: The screening record uses these DRE findings: normal; enlarged, smooth; nodular; hard (indurated); not performed.

sections.heading: What the findings mean for assessment
sections.body: A nodular or hard (indurated) prostate raises the suspicion of cancer and is usually a reason for further evaluation. An enlarged, smooth prostate is common with benign enlargement. A normal DRE does not rule out cancer, so the finding is interpreted together with PSA and imaging.

sources.name: European Association of Urology: EAU Guidelines on Prostate Cancer
US National Cancer Institute: Prostate Cancer Screening (PDQ), health professional version

articles.title: Reading the AI report in this app

sections.heading: What the AI report is
sections.body: The AI report is decision support for a qualified clinician, not a diagnosis. It combines the modules that could run for the patient (clinical values, MRI, slides) into a probability with a range, and a grade group when slides were analysed. Modules that could not run are listed with the reason.

sections.heading: Development mock data
sections.body: Until the trained models are added, every report is labelled "DEVELOPMENT MOCK DATA — NOT A CLINICAL RESULT." Its numbers are practice output and must not be used for patient care.

sections.heading: Explanations and accuracy figures
sections.body: Explanations (Grad-CAM heatmaps for images and SHAP values for clinical values) appear only when a real model produces them; otherwise the report says why they are not available. Accuracy and fairness figures appear only from stored evaluation runs; until then the report says that evaluation data is not yet available.
